newsitem.title: USA: U.N. okays three more Iraq contracts, total now 16.
newsitem.headline: U.N. okays three more Iraq contracts, total now 16.

text.p: The United Nations said Friday that it has approved another three contracts under the Iraq "oil-for-food" scheme, bringing the total approved so far to 16.

There are no contracts pending, according to a U.N. spokesman. However, Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) has signed contracts with at least another four companies and is in negotiations with another three, according to oil industry sources.

The U.N. wouldn't give any further information on the contracts, but of the three approved one is believed to be the one Mobil Corp signed on Wednesday with SOMO to lift 60,000 barrels per month of Basrah Light crude from the Gulf port of Mina-al-Bakr and another for Japan's Mitsubishi Corp to lift 40,000 barrels a day.

Sources said that U.N. overseers of the scheme have been slowing up processing the contracts as the total amount signed by SOMO has reached a level that could exceed the allowed $2 billion of sales over six months if current high prices were sustained.
The overseers maintain an option to cut back the amount contracted to maintain a cushion in order to keep the deal within its boundaries, U.N. sources said.
